newsitem.title: USA: U.S., North Korea discuss sub case, food, energy.
newsitem.headline: U.S., North Korea discuss sub case, food, energy.

text.p: The United States said on Tuesday it was discussing with North Korea an apology from Pyongyang over a submarine intrusion into South Korea as well as future food aid and energy supplies to North Korea.
But U.S. officials denied a newspaper report that a package deal was imminent involving these and other elements.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said Korea desk director Mark Minton met on Monday and on Tuesday at the United Nations with Li Hyong Chol, director of American affairs at the North Korean foreign ministry.
Earlier, Secretary of State Warren Christopher said in response to a reporter's question that food aid and energy supplies to North Korea were on the agenda.
"We have a wide variety of matters to discuss with them including the matters you've mentioned," he said before talks with Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini.
"I will emphasise the importance of the North Koreans expressing regret or making some other gesture with respect to the submarine incident in South Korea," Christopher said.
"That's an incident that does require some action or comment from the North Koreans before we can proceed."

A North Korean submarine intruded in September into South Korean waters and 22 crewmen were killed by South Korean troops or found dead. The incident greatly heightened tensions on the Korean peninsula.

The newspaper USA Today reported on Tuesday that a deal was "almost done" in which flood-stricken North Korea would receive food and energy assistance in return for a statement of regret over the submarine.

It said North Korea would also agree to four-party talks on the future of Korea, South Korea would resume building nuclear reactors in the North, and the United States and North Korea would discuss Pyongyang's alleged missile exports.
But spokesman Burns told a news briefing: "I personally am not aware of any package being put together." Other officials described the report as "not accurate" but did not elaborate.

Burns did confirm that the four-party talks proposal, floated by the United States and South Korea in April, was on the agenda along with a 1994 U.S.-North Korean nuclear pact, part of which provides for U.S. supplies of oil to Pyongyang.
The United Nations is a regular venue for talks between the United States and North Korea which have no diplomatic relations. They have been held frequently in recent months.
